unit_09.step.001.explanation: Earth is our planet, and the Sun is a star. The Moon has no light of its own. Never look straight at the Sun, because it can hurt your eyes.

unit_09.step.003.explanation: Earth is round, and much of it is covered in water. We can live here. Our heat and light come from the Sun.

unit_09.step.004.explanation: The Sun is a star that gives us heat and light.

unit_09.step.005.explanation: The Sun gives us light and heat. Its light helps us see, and its heat keeps us warm.

unit_09.step.006.explanation: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon. He went there in 1969.

unit_09.step.007.explanation: The visor protects your eyes, gloves protect your hands, and boots protect your feet. The oxygen pack helps you breathe because there is no air on the Moon.
unit_09.step.007.hint: Think about which part protects each body part, and which part helps the astronaut breathe.

unit_09.step.010.explanation: The Sun gives us daylight and helps plants grow. Plants need its light to make their food.
unit_09.step.010.hint: Remember what sunshine does for plants and what helps you see in the daytime.

unit_09.step.011.explanation: The lines join the stars into your own picture. You can make a shape and give it a name.

unit_09.step.012.explanation: Earth is a planet, and its water makes it look mostly blue. The Sun is a star. An astronomer studies stars. The Moon has no air to breathe.
